evaluation: Offline semantic assessment of complete actual prose, artifact DAG, object and message history and current receipt versions. Runtime success is factual only; no keyword grading.

goals.title: Stable road-use purpose and compatible product branch
necessary_conditions: Moving tourism remains shared-lane M6; no full closure or stopped live-lane advertising. Product capture is actually L2 with accepted parks scope or accepted studio.
Actual chosen capture/location and dependent paid content match lawful branch; optional grant precedes lay-by use, no grant needed for studio.

checks.condition: Moving tourism remains shared-lane M6; no full closure or stopped live-lane advertising. Product capture is actually L2 with accepted parks scope or accepted studio.

source_evidence.quote: Operate the permitted moving tourism ride, not a full road closure. Get barriers actually delivered before marshal deployment and actually returned afterwards. Deliver a current rider briefing and marshal packet before assembly, repair public notice and partner-held call sheet, ingest the privately held road camera card, and deliver two different outputs: the selected tourism cut with accessible captions, and the separately commissioned paid clothing product clip with its own accessible captions. Use authorized lay-by stationary product capture or the accepted studio alternative; do not cancel the moving ride or substitute a paid clip for tourism. Execute the cost/use record and send partner/ride lead actual current materials. Do not attach private raw card to public exports or transfer it as returned equipment. Marshal deployment verified70; briefs/call sheet65; barrier return115; both content placements verified120; private final140.

Permit M6 allows continuous moving tourism filming on Coast Road’s eastbound shared lane with six marshals and the booked barriers. It grants no full closure, stopped repeated product takes or stationary advertising setup in that live lane. Optional separate lay-by L2 stationary product use may be requested from parks, reply7; the grant cannot broaden M6. Accepted studio product capture needs no road-use extension. Both paid alternatives preserve the moving tourism ride and actual barrier/marshal obligations.

Tourism cut: a moving group on the shared Coast Road lane, marshals at the signed junctions, coastal view, volunteer credit; explain other road users retain access. Paid product clip: mannequin clothing seam/zip/pocket details, explicit paid label, no assertion of measured cycling performance and no rider endorsement. Rider brief: moving only, obey marshals, shared lane, no stopping for product takes. Marshal packet: six positions at junctions J1–J6, keep shared access open, barriers at booked staging points only. Partner call sheet states the actual selected product location and moving-tourism separation.
